align.help:
usage: wgsextract align [-h] [--r1 R1] [--r2 R2]
                        [--platform {illumina,dnbseq,ultima,pacbio,hifi,clr,ont,nanopore}]
                        [--aligner {auto,bwa,bwa-mem2,minimap2,pbmm2}] [--sample SAMPLE]
                        [--format {BAM,CRAM}] [--input-ref INPUT_REF] [--help-all]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --r1 R1               Read 1 FASTQ file
  --r2 R2               Read 2 FASTQ file (optional)
  --platform {illumina,dnbseq,ultima,pacbio,hifi,clr,ont,nanopore}
                        Sequencing platform; selects platform-specific alignment tooling (default:
                        detected from read groups or read names, else illumina).
  --aligner {auto,bwa,bwa-mem2,minimap2,pbmm2}
                        Aligner to use. Auto uses bwa-mem2 for short reads when the reference has
                        its index (see `ref index`), else bwa; for long reads pbmm2 for PacBio
                        when installed, otherwise minimap2.
  --sample SAMPLE       Sample name for the read group (default: the reads' file name).
  --format {BAM,CRAM}   Output format
  --input-ref INPUT_REF
                        Reference FASTA a CRAM --r1 was encoded with (default: --ref when its
                        sequence names, lengths and MD5s match the CRAM).
  --help-all            Show this help with the advanced options too, and exit.

global options:
  -i/--input, -o/--outdir, --genome, --ref, -t/--threads, -m/--memory, --json, --quiet, --debug,
  --config and the other global options are accepted before or after the command; 'wgsextract
  --help' lists them all.

4 advanced options not shown; 'wgsextract align --help-all' lists them.

examples:
  wgsextract align --r1 sample_R1.fastq.gz --r2 sample_R2.fastq.gz --ref hs38.fa
  wgsextract align --r1 hifi_reads.fastq.gz --preset map-hifi --ref hs38.fa

outputs (in the output directory unless noted):
  <reads stem>_aligned.bam or .cram (+ index).

needs:
  samtools; depending on options and inputs, also: bcftools, bwa, bwa-mem2,
  curl, gatk, minimap2, pbmm2, sambamba, samblaster; hours on a 30x genome.

bam.help:
usage: wgsextract bam [-h] <command> ...

positional arguments:
  <command>
    sort      Sort alignments by genomic coordinates. Required by almost all downstream tools
              (like variant callers) to function correctly.
    index     Create a random-access index (.bai/.crai) for your file. This allows tools to jump
              to specific regions instantly without reading the whole file.
    unindex   Remove the index file associated with your BAM/CRAM. Use this to force a re-indexing
              or to clean up workspace.
    unsort    Mark the file as 'unsorted' in the header. Rarely needed, but useful if a tool
              requires a specific header state for processing.
    to-cram   Convert BAM to the modern CRAM format. Highly recommended for long-term storage as
              it is ~30-50% smaller than BAM without losing data.
    to-bam    Convert a CRAM file back to the traditional BAM format. Useful if you need to use an
              older tool that doesn't support CRAM.
    unalign   Extract raw reads from a BAM/CRAM back into FASTQ format. Use this if you want to
              re-align your data to a different reference genome.
    identify  Analyze your BAM header to determine exactly which reference genome was used for the
              original alignment.
    merge     Merge several coordinate-sorted BAM/CRAM files (e.g. per-lane files) aligned to the
              same reference into one indexed file.
    to-ubam   Convert an aligned BAM/CRAM or FASTQ reads into a queryname-sorted unaligned BAM
              (uBAM) for GATK pipelines.

basecall.help:
usage: wgsextract basecall [-h] [--model MODEL] [--modified-bases CODES] [--device DEVICE]
                           [--read-ids FILE] [--regions-bed BED] [--alignment BAM]
                           [--models-dir MODELS_DIR] [--dorado-path DORADO_PATH]

Basecall Nanopore POD5 signal with ONT's Dorado (optional; install it yourself) into an unaligned
BAM that keeps the MM/ML methylation tags and feeds `align --r1`. Picks the GPU (Apple silicon,
else NVIDIA) or CPU, downloads hac/sup models into the wgsextract cache, and can re-basecall only
a panel's reads with sup.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --model MODEL         Dorado model: fast, hac or sup (optionally pinned, e.g. sup@v5.2.0; picked
                        for the run's chemistry), or a model folder (default: hac)
  --modified-bases CODES
                        Also call base modifications, e.g. 5mCG_5hmCG (CpG methylation) or
                        5mC_5hmC; comma-separated for several. Writes MM/ML tags.
  --device DEVICE       auto (Apple silicon GPU, else an NVIDIA GPU nvidia-smi lists, else CPU),
                        cpu, metal, cuda:all or cuda:<id>[,<id>...] (default: auto)
  --read-ids FILE       Basecall only the reads named in this file (one read ID per line).
  --regions-bed BED     Re-basecall only the reads --alignment places in these regions (a panel
                        BED), e.g. with --model sup.
  --alignment BAM       Aligned BAM/CRAM of the same run whose reads in --regions-bed are re-
                        basecalled.
  --models-dir MODELS_DIR
                        Folder Dorado downloads models into and reuses them from (default: config
                        dorado_models_directory, else the wgsextract cache's dorado-models)
  --dorado-path DORADO_PATH
                        Path to the dorado executable (optional if in PATH)

global options:
  -i/--input, -o/--outdir, --genome, --ref, -t/--threads, -m/--memory, --json, --quiet, --debug,
  --config and the other global options are accepted before or after the command; 'wgsextract
  --help' lists them all.

examples:
  wgsextract basecall --input pod5/ --modified-bases 5mCG_5hmCG
  wgsextract basecall --input pod5/ --model sup --regions-bed panel.bed --alignment sample_aligned.bam
  wgsextract basecall --input reads.pod5 --device cpu --model fast

outputs (in the output directory unless noted):
  <POD5 file or folder stem>.<model>[.<modifications>][.subset].bam: unaligned
  reads with Dorado's tags (MM/ML with --modified-bases), beside the POD5
  input or in --outdir.

needs:
  dorado, samtools; hours for a MinION flow cell on a GPU.
